adjudicated.jp: 沈んだ日。その光だけが、空をよじのぼって。
adjudicated.en: The sun had sank. Only its light, now, clambers up in the sky.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese presents the sun as already set and its light climbing the sky in one past-tense image. The English uses the ungrammatical past participle 'sank' after 'had' and abruptly shifts the light into present tense.
adjudicated.remedy: The sun had sunk. Only its light climbed up the sky.

withheld.jp: 有識者数が少ないからね」
withheld.en:
Taichi: "Back then things were quiiite a bit snug. The number of 'Experts' was really low, that's why."
* 'Expert' = person in which the basic emotions (happiness, fear, sorrow, pleasure) are present.
comments: See CCA0009B and more. Never established as Gunjou slang or used consistently, but the reactions below seem to hint at this. Expanded. Miki is described explicitly as an Expert. Curiously, the ruby text says it's "ushiki", but Youshikisha (reading of 有識者) is actually a world, while Ushiki[sha] doesn't seem to be. Could be "possibly intelligent/well informed person", making the term more sarcastic. Scare quotes to make the term scarier and terrifying. -GHS
